items.note: S3.2.1 says a network exchanges two banks with signs and restores auxiliary values, and S3.2.2 names three-element subsets, gather/scatter and cancelling auxiliary wires, but the eight-row schedule, y_S -> y_S + x_S and the map (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a) are never given.

S3.2.1 alludes to invertible frames D_v 'cancelling across the network' but gives neither the commutation of a common frame with a pointwise gate nor the endpoint operator D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}.

S3.2.2 names nested subspaces attached to gates (and quotes the lemma's opening line 997) but states none of its content: no triple indicator orthogonality, no L = Ich, no sum Wm - 2N + 2L, no L < N/2.

S3.3's method 'instantiate the bit network with rational subspaces and implement edges by address shears' alludes to the interface, but the endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w) = I_m and s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b are absent.

S3.4's method names 'the complex phase network' and S3.4.2 names phase frames, but the frames C_U, the product of translation kernels aI + bX_v per residual vector, s_c and the C^{tensor m} endpoint are not stated.

The plan states the key inequality s < Wm (S3.2.2) and s/W < m as the source of the saving (S3.2.3), and quotes s/W < m^tau (S3.3.2), matching lines 167-174; it gives neither the two networks' separate s_b, s_c, the deficits, the reason L < N/2, nor the explicit tau = sigma = 1 - 2^{-50}.
Named only through the 'controlled-shifts' dependency of S3.3, S3.3.1 and S3.4.3; no step states the linear-cost stream operations or controlled shifts.

S3.3.1 states the lower-triangular times partial-permutation times lower-triangular factorization and a cost 'by rank', but omits invertibility of E_1, E_2, the exactly-a ones in Pi, and the exact cost (a interchanges plus O(V)); it also writes the shear as (H,D) -> (H+D,D) rather than the edge shear (H,D) -> (H+AD,D) whose rank is the count.

S3.2.3 gives the recurrence in words (s calls at parameter f on volume V/W, ratio s/W < m) and S3.3.2 the O(Vu^tau) outcome; the power-width form e = m^k with a row field divisible by W^k, the per-node O(1) normalized overhead, and the completion of the shear H <- H+D into an interchange are missing. Unsure between stated and mentioned; no derivation sub-steps follow the paper's 1491-1616 proof.

S3.3 states the O(Vu^tau) interchange of two disjoint contiguous u-bit fields with fixed tau < 1, as in lines 95-97, but omits that the addresses form a complete Cartesian product; the reduction from arbitrary to power widths (row field, padding, base-m pieces) is not shown, so it is not credited as derived.

S3.4.2 describes the idea (phase frames, smaller groups of selected bits, binary changes of basis) without the conjugation by P_M, the s_c child calls of C^{tensor f}, the inverse-kernel identity or H_0^{tensor D} = b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D.

S3.4.3 gives the operation and the deterministic repair of exceptional addresses, but says it 'costs linear time', whereas the lemma's bound is O(V(L^tau + 1)) (lines 2001-2009) and the change of basis costs O(V((eK)^tau + 1)) (lines 2224-2226), driven by chunk swaps of cost O(VL^tau).

Only the generic recurrence of S3.2.3 applies; the layer's recurrence F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau + 1), its leaves at e < d^beta, the row index from the first q_0 chunks and the unrolling to d^{lambda'} are absent.

S3.4 and S3.4.4 state the H_0 layer on selected bits of at most d chunks at cost O(Vd^{lambda'}), and S3.4.1 the exact Gaussian dyadics with one final truncation; the same-position selection in K-bit chunks, the output Q_p(Hz) with error < sqrt2 2^{-p} and the guard-width bound are missing. The children (S3.4.1-S3.4.3) list ingredients but omit the recurrence and guard widths, and S3.4.4 restates S3.4, so I do not credit a derivation (conservative).
S4.5.1 says powers of y serve as roots so twiddles are signed shifts and the frequency order is retained, but not F_t^+ F_t^- = t^{-1} I, the bit-reversed order, the layout L, the error or the cost.
S4.5.2 names signed packing (Kronecker substitution) with the established O(n log n) multiplier, but gives no packing base, no output Q_p(fg/r) and no cost O(rp log(rp)).
S4.5 describes transform, pointwise product, opposite transform in general terms; the normalization (f*g)/(rM), the common LB order identity, the error sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p} and the cost are absent.
S4.2 matches lines 188-192 in words, but the identity P_s F_s = 2^{2 alpha^2} B_0 P_t F_t A, the condition theta > p/alpha^4 and the tensor form are not given.

S4.3 names Bluestein's identity turning the middle transform into a cyclic convolution with chirp phases, without the formula QF_t u = conj(a)(a*(conj(a) u))/T; the cancellation of the source permutation R (eq:source-permutation-cancel) is not stated anywhere in the plan.
S5.2 alludes to 'a compatible choice of rational parameters' and S0 gives kappa = 2^{-182}, but no other exponent, size (b, p = 6b, d, K, T) or prime choice is given.
S4.1 names a Chinese-remainder address map onto distinct prime cyclic axes that preserves convolution, without Phi: x -> prod x_i^{mu_i} or the triangular digit formula.
S4.4 paraphrases lines 196-198; the map x_d -> zeta y with zeta = e^{pi i/r}, the wrap check and M_C = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) are not given.
The overall flow is alluded to in S0, S4 and S5.1, but the source transform 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A = R F_s, its conjugate and the six-step algorithm with the scales S and 2^{2b+4}S are not given.

S5.1 says the recovered coefficient error is strictly below 1/2 and carries give the product, following lines 208-211, but none of the error quantities (E_s, E_w, 448b 2^{-b+gamma}) or the role of p = 6b and gamma <= b/4 appear.
S5.2 says the parameters make all cost-table terms fit O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}), without the table entries, the margins g_1..g_7 or min g_i = 2^{-181} = 2 kappa.

S6 states that the power saving gives limit zero for T_A(n)/(n lg n), refuting the n log n lower bound in this model, as at line 386; the quantifier form (eventual bound c_A n lg n for every machine, negated by liminf 0) is left implicit.

errors.says: Packed selected-bit addition across rectangles 'costs linear time' with a deterministic repair.
errors.paper: The lemma's time is O(V(L^tau+1) + M A^3 + delta_bad M A (R+A)), i.e. O(V(L^tau+1)) in the family, because it uses chunk swaps of cost O(VL^tau); a fixed change of basis costs O(V((eK)^tau+1)), the node overhead of the layer recurrence.

errors.says: The lower-triangular factorization makes 'an address shear (H,D) -> (H+D,D)' cost by rank.
errors.paper: The factorization prices the edge shears (H,D) -> (H+AD,D) at exactly rank(A) interchanges plus O(V); H <- H+D is the endpoint shear produced by the whole network on every role, not one priced by the factorization (it would be full rank m).

errors.says: Only a power saving in the log factor can beat n log n (S0's motivation likewise says beating n log n needs a power saving).
errors.paper: The paper says only that it obtains a strict power saving in the logarithmic factor; any o(log n) factor would beat n log n, and refuting the eventual lower bound only needs liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n) = 0.

errors.says: Both tape procedures come from a (single) fixed linear network; S3's method says 'one linear-network construction', and S3.2.1 speaks of 'a fixed linear network'.
errors.paper: Each procedure arises from its own fixed network: a bit network with rational labels and a complex network with Gaussian dyadic values and binary labels, sharing the same construction pattern.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route at the level of the introduction: digit convolution, two network-based tape procedures with s < Wm and a recursive saving, the CRT/resampling/chirp/twist/synthetic-ring reductions, then exact recovery and cost accounting. Below that it thins out. The network construction (schedule, labels, L < N/2), the two interfaces, the recurrences with their node overheads, the guard widths, the error budget and the margin computation are only named. The packed-addition cost is misstated as linear, and the cancellation of the retained source permutation R is never stated, so the link from S4.2 to S5 is missing.
